title: Book 4 — Melpomene, Chapter 184
paragraphs: From the Garamantes, at another distance of ten days' journey, there is another hill of salt and spring of water, with people living around it called the Atarantes, who alone of all men we know are nameless: for while collectively they have the name Atarantes, no individual among them has any name given to him. These curse the sun when it is at its height, reviling it with every kind of foul name because it oppresses them with its burning heat—both themselves and their land. After this, at a distance of ten days' journey, there is another hill of salt and spring of water, with people living around it. Near this salt-hill is a mountain called Atlas, which is small in circumference and rounded on every side; and so exceedingly high is it said to be that its summits cannot be seen, for clouds never leave them either in summer or in winter. This mountain, the natives say, is the pillar of the sky. From this mountain these people get their name: they are called Atlanteans; and it is said that they neither eat anything that has life nor have any dreams.
